title: It's hard out there for a game-dev
author: cumbiaowl
selftext:
So, we have AI now that makes it super easy to build games. But a good game? One that you're proud of and doesn't give you the jitters or riles up your insecurities when you publish it? This is pretty hard. 

Anyhow, I thought building Skippers would be easy and super fast. But it wasn't. It's a simple game but it took me about 3 days to polish it enough to make me proud, jitter-free, and less insecure of it. 

Check it out, some of you may remember a show about nothing when playing it: [https://skippers.gg](https://skippers.gg) 

[Skippers first reveal](https://reddit.com/link/1w3h3xf/video/qmhbvzzzaqmh1/player)

comments.author: Sudden-Fix-6336
comments.body: Honest questions. When you built this game what were you trying to achieve that wasnt already done with frogger? What are you proud about here? How did you give it your own cool spin? How is it pushing that genre of game forward? I think AI devs need to ask themselves these questions before starting a game.

replies.author: cumbiaowl
replies.body:
\- trying to achieve: a throwback arcade game that people would enjoy playing for short periods of time in their browser  
\- something that hasn’t been done before: no, I wasn’t going for this, I’m ok with this, and frankly, most games out there are repetitions of previous games/books/etc. and they do great… this is fine  
\- proud of what: I like playing it  
\- pushing the genre of game forward: not sure what genre you’re referring to, but I don’t have a goal of pushing a genre forward… games to me are meant for enjoyment 

I appreciate the questions!

replies.author: Sudden-Fix-6336
replies.body: All of my questions were linked to "So, we have AI now that makes it super easy to build games. But a good game? One that you're proud of and doesn't give you the jitters or riles up your insecurities when you publish it? This is pretty hard." Its VERY easy to make replicas of games out. Its difficult to do the things I asked about. My point is you are going to get a lot of hate from people if you dont try to do anything innovative. Good luck on your game building journey.

replies.author: cumbiaowl
replies.body:
That’s fair. Not concerned with hate at all.

Thanks

replies.author: cumbiaowl
replies.body: Yeah, a bit of an oxymoron but there are new standards now

comments.author: Time_Cat_5212
comments.body:
I made this game, and I wasn't sure how people would react to it.  Would it be called AI slop?  Would they see the 14 hour days I put in over the last 3 months, or all of my original creative vision?

"Blocky" is a geometric puzzle game. The player has to move and rotate descending blocks so that they fit into a stack of other blocks, and if the stack reaches the top of the page, it's game over.  I thought really long and hard about how I wanted the blocks to work, how I wanted scoring to work, and I decided to ignore the critics and just go with my intuition.

Well anyway tl;dr, here's the game.

*Literally Tetris*

comments.author: IcyBother8850
comments.body: Bro maybe try using AI to achive something previously not possible by a single dev. Whats the point of doing a frogger clone did it teach you anything?

replies.author: cumbiaowl
replies.body:
The point: learning gamedev (I’m new to it), prompting techniques, AI workflows, what makes people tick, etc. 

Thanks for commenting!

comments.author: Antique_Pair_140
comments.body: Haha what a flashback! It plays just like it should—classic retro arcade vibes and music straight out of an old bar machine. I gotta admit, I couldn't get past level ONE... jumped right in and died instantly! If it were a real coin-op back in the day, that's when you'd smash the glass with a beer bottle haha (remember when some machines had metal mesh so people wouldn't break the screen?). Thumbs up!
